Chapter 9. The Trickster’s Lesson: Embracing Paradox.
Life, as the Lakota have long known, is packed with contradictions. And no one embodies that better than the trickster—sometimes showing up as a clever coyote, sometimes as a crafty spider. You’ll find him in countless stories, always flipping things upside down and reminding people that nothing’s ever as simple as it looks.
If you’re someone who craves certainty, the trickster can feel pretty frustrating—always dodging a straight answer. But if you’re willing to laugh at yourself, he’s actually a teacher, nudging you to see beyond the obvious.
Picture this: A respected elder is asked to explain the meaning of a sacred ceremony. But instead of giving a direct answer, he launches into a story about a time he got hopelessly lost in the woods... and ended up learning a lot more from his mistakes than from the times things went smoothly. The listeners can’t help but laugh, but the message sticks with them. Wisdom isn’t about having every answer—it’s about staying open to being surprised.
And it’s not just in old stories. The trickster’s spirit shows up all the time in daily life. Plans fall apart, expectations get turned on their head, and even when you think you’ve got everything mapped out, life throws in a twist. Like a family heading out to pick wild berries, only to get caught in a sudden storm. They come home drenched and empty-handed, but laughing harder than they have in ages. That’s when you realize—real joy isn’t found in perfection, but in being willing to embrace the messiness.
The trickster also brings us a gentle lesson in humility. Nobody is above making mistakes—we all do it. These stories invite us to laugh at ourselves, to forgive others, and to remember that even the wisest among us can get fooled now and then. In a world that pushes us to be certain and stay in control, the trickster offers a different way—one that values curiosity, play, and the guts to admit when you’re wrong.
So, if you look at life through the trickster’s eyes, all those contradictions and surprises? They turn into chances to grow. The Lakota way isn’t about dodging paradox. It’s about learning to dance with it.
